notes: METHOD. Wikimedia Commons API only (no video file downloaded): about 110 file-namespace searches (filetype:video with boxing terms in English, Russian, German, French, Spanish, Dutch, Italian, Finnish, Swedish, Polish, Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Thai, Arabic, Persian, plus deepcategory: on Boxing, Boxers, Boxing by country, Boxing venues, Kickboxing, Muay Thai, Savate) gave 2,454 distinct files; 174 passed a boxing keyword filter; each kept clip's licence was read from its own page (imageinfo extmetadata plus the page wikitext) and three or more still thumbnails were viewed. The later searches returned almost no new files, so the Commons pool is close to exhausted.

CATEGORY NAMES. The only real video category is 'Category:Videos of boxing' (34 files). 'Videos of amateur boxing', 'Boxing videos', 'Videos of savate', 'Videos of boxing training' and 'Videos of kickboxing' do not exist; 'Videos of Muay Thai' has 6 files.

DAY OF THE TOWN SERIES (Zelio007, CC BY-SA 4.0). The 2017-09-09 set has only two 'Russian boxing' clips (0025, 0029) and one 'Kickboxing' clip (0046); the rest of the 47 'Day of the Town' videos are BMX, skateboarding, puppetry, dance and street scenes. The category listing itself was rate-limited (HTTP 429) on the day, so this rests on the title search.

PUBLIC DOMAIN GROUPS. (a) US military via DVIDS, tagged PD-USGov-Military-Army / -Air Force (8 clips). (b) Dutch Polygoon newsreels 1931-1949 released by the Netherlands Institute for Sound and Vision through Open Beelden, tagged PD-old-70 with a Public Domain Mark (13 clips). (c) US films of 1891-1907 tagged PD-US-expired / PD-old (Edison, Dickson, Heise, Miles Brothers; 15 clips). (d) Two US-government films of 1945 on the Internet Archive. PD-USGov and PD-US-expired are statements about US law.

SHAREALIKE. 16 clips are ShareAlike (CC BY-SA 2.5 CO, 3.0, 3.0 NL, 4.0). Cut or annotated excerpts of them that are distributed must carry the same licence; whether a trained model or a label file is an 'adaptation' is a legal question to settle before these go in. The best technique footage found (the six EVD-boxeo lessons) is ShareAlike.

MINORS. 7 clips are flagged minors=yes from the title, description, categories or the frames, and 10 are 'unknown'. The two 'Russian boxing' clips show headgear and young-looking boxers and may well be under-18 bouts. The Slovenian 2016 national championship is mixed: youth bouts first, adult men later.

PEOPLE AND MARKS. None of the listed pages carries a personality-rights or trademark warning template. That is not consent: a copyright licence does not cover the image rights of identifiable boxers, referees or spectators, and the TV-sourced clips carry channel logos (TV Urslja, Patriotic Forces of Donbass TV).

LICENCE REVIEW. YouTube- and Vimeo-sourced clips kept in the list all show a passed review on the page (a named reviewer or the review bot). Three old films carry an unconfirmed {{LicenseReview}} tag but are public domain by age (1891, 1894, 1897). YouTube-sourced files whose review is still pending were moved to 'rejected'.

SIZES. size_mb is decimal megabytes of the original file on Commons. Two files are over 1 GB on their own (Slovenian championship 2.5 GB, Yekaterinburg fist-fight 1.04 GB). Commons also serves smaller transcodes (240p-1080p WebM) of every file, which would cut the totals several-fold.

DUPLICATES. Several old films exist in two or three copies (Corbett and Courtney x4 incl. 'Boxing 1892' and 'James J Corbett 1894', Leonard-Cushing x2, Gordon Sisters x2, Men Boxing x2, Quentemeyer-Fouguet x2, Corbett-Fitzsimmons x2); the weaker copies carry a 'duplicate_of' field; dropping them removes 6 entries.

INTERNET ARCHIVE. 408 boxing-titled movie items carry a CC or public-domain licence field, but that field is typed by the uploader: most CC0 / PD-Mark hits are video-game recordings or ripped TV broadcasts. Only two US-government films and one CC BY gym clip were credible enough to list; frames of these three were not viewed.

MORE US-MILITARY FOOTAGE. dvidshub.net holds many more boxing videos (unit 'smokers', service-academy and garrison tournaments) than the 8 copied to Commons. Its search page refused automated access on the day (empty HTTP 202), so none are listed; each DVIDS video page states its own public-domain status and must be read one by one.

YOUTUBE FILTER. Search, then Filters > Features > Creative Commons. With the Data API: search.list with type=video and videoLicense=creativeCommon, then confirm each hit with videos.list part=status (status.license must be 'creativeCommon'). YouTube offers one CC licence only, CC BY (never NC or ND), but the tag is set by the uploader: accept it only when the channel is clearly the maker (a club, a federation, a broadcaster's own channel), never for re-uploaded fights.

VIMEO FILTER. Search, then the Licence filter: keep 'CC BY', 'CC BY-SA' and 'CC0'; drop every option containing NC or ND. The API exposes the same value in each video's 'license' field (by, by-sa, cc0 against by-nc, by-nd, by-nc-sa, by-nc-nd). The Yle Archives clips in this list came to Commons from Vimeo that way.

NOT VERIFIED. (1) Nothing was watched in full: content, minors and usefulness scores rest on three to eight still frames and the page text. (2) That the Commons account 'Evdcoldeportes' really is Colombia's sports ministry (the EVD-boxeo source site deportes.gov.co is cited but there is no review tag). (3) Ages of boxers marked 'unknown'. (4) Whether the YouTube/Vimeo originals still carry the CC licence today (Commons records the licence at review time; CC licences are not revocable). (5) Whether TV-produced clips contain third-party footage. (6) Public-domain status outside the United States for the US-law rationales.
